issues.text: The method is largely a combination of existing techniques, so its novelty is limited; the main contribution is the consistency and normality result, and the evaluator says applicability is not universal because those results depend on strong assumptions.
issues.quote:
The method is mostly a clever combination of existing methods; the main
contribution is showing \[the\] consistency and normality of their
estimator.

issues.text: The strong assumptions underlying the consistency and asymptotic normality results (which depend on N) may not hold in other settings, so the method's applicability is limited.
issues.quote:
asymptotic arguments and
asymptotic results imply that they need not always hold (as they depend
on N)

issues.text: Finding a LASSO penalty sequence satisfying Assumption 5 appears non-trivial, and the paper offers no guidance on this despite its robustness checks.
issues.quote:
finding a
penalty sequence for the LASSO that fulfills Assumption 5 seems
non-trivial. Unless I've missed it, there seems no guidance in that
respect

issues.text: The simulation evidence for normality (approximately holding for n above about 3000) is the only guidance offered, and the paper does not indicate the settings in which the assumptions can be expected to hold, which limits its generalisability.
issues.quote:
A suggestion would thus be to provide some more intuition about the
settings in which the assumptions can be expected to hold

issues.text: Conceptually, pooling treatments that have no effect (pooling them with control) or grouping dosages based on LASSO selection may be inappropriate; the evaluator is unsure this should be allowed and thinks a discussion is needed.
issues.quote:
Scientifically, I am a bit unsure
whether this should be allowed; a discussion seems warranted. It is
obviously principled and data-driven, but conceptually, it seems wrong
to me.

issues.text: Practical adoption is uncertain because the techniques (the Jia and Rohe correction for correlated regressors and the Andrews et al. winner's curse correction) are technical, and no software implementation is provided.
issues.quote:
Unless there will be no software
implementation, I am unsure how much practitioners will \[adopt\] the
technique

issues.text: The interventions tested have been studied before, including by the authors and in the same dataset, which limits the novelty of the field study; this is disclosed only late in the paper (page 28).
issues.quote:
all tested interventions have been studied before,
including by the authors, and including in this very same dataset

issues.text: Data quality is described as excellent in the main text, but the appendix shows only 80% accuracy of names and dates of birth, unquantified fake records, and 71% of children with completely overlapping vaccines, which the evaluator considers far from excellent.
issues.quote:
In the main text, they
    describe the data quality as \"excellent\". In the appendix (p. 92),

issues.text: The substitution-effect tables in the online appendix are cut off because of landscape formatting, so notes and columns are missing and the content is hard to interpret, making it unclear whether incentive effects are substitution or genuinely new immunizations.
issues.quote:
the tables are in landscape format, but the relevant pages are not, and
hence about half of the tables/pages seem to be cut.

issues.text: The coding of the dependent variable in the substitution analysis is unclear, and the control means (up to .69) look implausibly high if the outcome equals 1 for children not in the register, which would need more discussion.
issues.quote:
However, the control means look incredibly high (up to .69) should
    the dependent variable really equal 1 if a child is not in the
    register.

issues.text: Section 4 is hard to follow, and it is unclear which subset of the data is finally analyzed.
issues.quote:
Section 4 could benefit from proofreading and streamlining. At the
    end, as a reader one is confused which sub-set of the data is
    finally analyzed.

issues.text: The pre-analysis plan (mentioned late, in a footnote) did not describe a systematic approach to interaction effects, and the shift from the planned analysis is not explained; the authors should comment on this change.
issues.quote:
A systematic approach like the
    current one did not seem to be the plan, however, not even in the
    updated pre-registration from 2018.
